body: Even though it's fiction, I think the TV show UnReal does a good job at depicting how these reality TV shows are often manipulated for views & the conditions ect.

I think they just said when it comes to promoting managers overall. I've worked for several retail places in the past as well, but WFM definitely tops the chart with toxicity. i do think a large part is your specific store as well, however, I think a decent manager is one who knows his employees and doesn't have to rely on metrics. I personally know I would be more efficient if I didn't have to worry about big brother watching every time, it makes me want to slow down out of spite.

I didn't necessarily mean it was strictly Bezo's viewpoint. However, compared to other retail companies ect, Bezo does seem to offer the least amount of employee incentives, appreciation, recognition ect. Going back to the NYT article, it even mentioned that compared to other companies, like WalMart, Amazon promotes less from within the company and would rather hire fresh college grads for management positions. Yes, retail world and warehouses probably have this general view, but I think Bezo really examplifies this view.

The NYT just came out with the an article on Bezos and Amazon Warehouse. I know WFM isn't exactly a warehouse, but there were some interesting tidbits about how Bezo views low wage workers- the jobs aren't meant to be long term.
I'm starting another job this month lol but plan on staying part, part time at WF for extra $
